messages.author: db6b7f5c26ead7f4
messages.subject: mixed argos and gps data
parts:
Hi Chris,
I'm trying to convert some combined argos and fastloc (gps) data into a telemetry object. So I've followed some previous advice and split the data into 2 separate data set to convert each one then tbind them back together. But when I bring the data back together the COV.x.x and COV.y.y are off by a factor or 2. I know there some some issue about the root 2 factor the for the semi major/minor argos conversion, etc. I'm just not sure if I should fix this in the gps UERE or it's fine as is. 

I can demo with the pelican data:

data(pelican)
uere(pelican) <- 10 #I'd like to fix this as I do for my data
ppp <- tbind(pelican)
ppp[1:6,]

if I look at row 4 (first gps) I would expect that COV.x.x (and COV.y.y) would be equal to (UERE * HDOP)^2 [ =(10*2)^2) ] but it is (UERE * HDOP)^2/2 same with the 6th row. In terms of the SSM I'd like to fix the error rates with the former. But I'm not sure if the tbind was just making them match the argos and that 2 will be accounted for in the ctmm functions, or should I adjust the UERE by a sqrt(2) factor. If this has been discussed before or there are descriptions of the telemetry object columns that will give the answer, just point me in that direction. 

Thanks!

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: mixed argos and gps data
parts:
Hi Devin,

Yes, sorry about the confusion. I am following the Argos and GPS convention of assigning and reporting the RMS UERE with the uere() methods and model-fit summary() reports on error estimates. This does differ by a sqrt(2) from the x-y standard deviation in two dimensions. The columns COV.x.x and COV.y.y are given by (UERE * HDOP)^2/2, as you have noticed. So, if you throw in a sqrt(2) on assignment, then that should do what you want.

Best,
Chris
